evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:743-762 — introspect_pm_token() conflates 'the PM token is genuinely inactive' with 'the introspection HTTP call failed'. On the cache-miss path, when the PM introspect endpoint returns a non-success status (`!response.status().is_success()` at line 755 — i.e. a transient 5xx / 429 / network blip, NOT a valid `{active:false}` body), the code executes `state.token_cache.set(token, false, None, None)` (line 758, comment 'Cache inactive tokens too (to prevent repeated failed validations)') and THEN returns Err. This poisons the 60s-TTL cache: a still-valid PM token is now cached as active=false.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:730-739 — the very next introspect_pm_token call for that same valid token within the TTL is served from cache and returns a SUCCESS value `TokenIntrospectionResponse { active: false, .. }` (no Err this time), so callers see 'token inactive' rather than 'introspection unavailable'.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:1067-1101 — blast radius in sync_session(): a cache-hit with active=false takes the `if !token_info.active` branch (line 1082) and calls `session_service.invalidate_session(portal_session)` — it actively TEARS DOWN the user's live portal session. Net effect: a single transient PM-API introspection failure force-logs-out a validly-authenticated user from the Reality Portal for up to the full cache TTL, with no way to recover until the poisoned entry expires.

Fix: only write a negative cache entry when PM returns a well-formed response that explicitly says active=false. On transport/HTTP-status failures, return Err WITHOUT calling token_cache.set(...) so transient upstream failures fail-open on caching (they still fail-closed on the individual request via the returned Err) instead of persisting a false 'inactive' verdict that later reads as an authoritative logout signal.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:682, 706, 743 — the three outbound SSO/OAuth helpers exchange_code_for_token(), get_user_info(), and introspect_pm_token() each build a fresh `reqwest::Client::new()` per invocation. `Client::new()` sets NO request timeout, so an unresponsive/hung PM OAuth endpoint blocks the SSO login / session-sync request indefinitely (Tokio task parked with no upper bound) on the auth hot path.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:757-762 — a correctly-configured shared client already exists: PmApiClient::new() builds `reqwest::Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_seconds)).build()` and is held on AppState as `pm_api_client` (state.rs:863). The SSO helpers ignore it and instantiate untimed, unpooled clients instead.

Impact: (1) no request timeout -> hung PM upstream stalls auth requests and can exhaust the server's task/connection budget under load; (2) per-call Client::new() creates a new connection pool each time, defeating keep-alive/TLS reuse and adding a fresh TLS handshake to every token exchange, userinfo, and introspection call.

Fix: reuse a single shared timed reqwest::Client (extend PmApiClient or add a dedicated pooled client to AppState) across exchange_code_for_token / get_user_info / introspect_pm_token, and ensure it carries an explicit .timeout(...) matching the existing PmApiClient config.
